summary: Argentina is in a quieter stretch under President Milei, but stocks are slipping. The Merval fell 1% to 94,530 on Oct 29, its fourth straight loss, while dollar bonds bounced and country risk eased back under 750 points (Ambito, Infobae). That is still above the 709 seen on Oct 22, so the trend in risk is up. Monthly inflation was 1.9% in September and yearly inflation 33.4%, and the IMF's third review is still open. Energy names ride Vaca Muerta output and oil above $100.
for_you: Argentina is a high risk, high swing market. YPF and VIST ride oil above $100. Keep any trade small, and check the inflation print on Oct 13 first.

summary: Lula won the Oct 25 runoff, and Brazil has now fallen four days in a row: the Ibovespa lost 1.06% to 169,186 on Oct 29 and the dollar rose 0.76% to R$5.39 on worries about Lula's spending plans (Agencia Brasil, Reuters via TradingView). The central bank decides Nov 3 to 4 with the Selic at 13.75%. Before the vote, economists expected a 0.25 point cut in November (Focus survey, Oct 23); since the result, rate futures jumped and analysts now debate a pause or even a hike, so sources disagree on what is priced (UOL, Estadao, InfoMoney). In New York on Oct 29 EWZ fell 1.43% to 33.14, BBD 3.66% to 2.63, and NU rose 0.67% to 12.05 (Massive). The test is still a credible spending plan from Lula's team before the decision.
for_you: No Brazil buys, swings or new puts until the Nov 3 to 4 decision. NU closed at 12.05 on Oct 29, 8.0% under its 13.10 'thesis broken' line, and stays Wait. An EWZ Nov 20 $37 put is 10.4% in the money at 33.14; with no verdict, do not roll.

summary: The US and China extended their trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. Mainland stocks stay weak: the CSI 300 fell 1.39% to 3,985.50 on Oct 30, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose about 1.5% late in the day (CNBC). The yuan stays near a four year high; the central bank set its midpoint at 6.7138 on Oct 30 (PBOC via TMGM). Q3 GDP grew 4.5% while shoppers stayed weak, and the record trade surplus raises the odds of a new tariff fight before Jan 10.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. A stronger yuan helps US exporters' China sales a little. No action; Chinese ADRs are not on the buy zone list.

summary: The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% on Oct 29 in a unanimous vote, but said a hike was debated, and markets price about a 67% chance of a hike in December (CNBC, LSEG). Euro area inflation is 3.8%, the highest since September 2023, with energy up 18.8%, and Dutch gas for December jumped to 101.63 euros on Oct 30, the highest since late 2022, with storage near 75% (CNBC). President Lagarde said she will step down on Feb 7, 2027, adding a leadership question to the rate path (CNBC). France's economy shrank 0.1% in Q3 amid unrest and a budget fight, while Shell and BP beat on refining (Insee via CNBC, Reuters). ASML is still the European name that matters most for the AI themes.
for_you: A December ECB hike would firm the euro, which helps US holders of European ADRs but hurts exporters. Energy is the pressure point: TTE and Shell gain, while European industry and BUD pay. No European name is a setup; European bank ADRs (SAN, ING) stay a wait.

country: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
summary: The US-Iran war that began Feb 28, 2026 is in a tense pause before the US midterms. Gulf crude exports have recovered, averaging 24.6 million barrels a day in the week to Oct 18, above the pre war level (Kpler via Al Jazeera), yet Brent rose 2.4% to $117.62 on Oct 30 after a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by explosive devices and Houthi rebels said they struck Saudi refineries at Ras Tanura and Rabigh and a site at Abqaiq (Reuters). Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Oct 30, and Iran has not answered a letter from Vice President Vance (Reuters). Traders and analysts still expect possible US strikes after Nov 3. Most Gulf champions are not US listed, so the US trade runs through producers, refiners, LNG exporters and the KSA ETF.
for_you: XOM and CVX reported strong refining profits; manage them by the 2R targets, not by hope. Do not add oil names into the Nov 3 vote: a strike could spike prices, a deal could drop Brent toward $80 (Goldman via Economic Times).

summary: India's central bank raised its repo rate 0.25 point to 5.50% on Oct 7, its first hike since February 2023, as oil above $100 pushed inflation up. Stocks held up while the rest of Asia fell: on Oct 30 the Nifty rose 0.51% to 23,053.10 and the Sensex 0.42% to 74,459.53, led by IT and pharma, and both gained nearly 2% for the week (Business Line). Foreign exchange reserves fell for a seventh straight week to an over two month low (Reuters). Brent back near $117 is the main threat to an oil importer. A 10% US tariff still applies to most Indian goods.
for_you: India helps outsourcers (INFY, WIT) through a weak rupee and hurts banks and travel through higher rates. INDA closed at 47.41 on Oct 29 (Massive) with no verdict; low priority.

The Nikkei fell 2.12% to 63,290.11 on Oct 30, ending a four day run, as US tech results hit chip names: Advantest fell 5.43%, Tokyo Electron 3.93% and SoftBank 4.66% (CNBC). The yen is near 157 per dollar, still weak enough to help exporters. Higher rates help the big banks.
for_you: No action. A December BOJ hike is now the base case, which can lift the yen and jolt US tech for a day or two. EWJ closed at 94.94 on Oct 29 (Massive); no Japan name is a setup.

summary: The peso weakened 1.2% to about 18.86 per dollar on Oct 29 as strong US growth and inflation revived bets on another Fed hike (TMGM). Banxico holds at 6.50%, and Deputy Governor Galia Borja called that a 'good monetary position' with inflation moving toward 3%, though 'the job is not yet done' (TMGM). Q3 GDP is due Oct 30, with forecasts of 0.7% growth on the quarter and 2.5% on the year. The USMCA was not renewed in July and moved to annual reviews, so trade rules for cars and factories stay uncertain. A weaker peso cuts the dollar value of Mexican profits but lowers costs for companies that make goods in Mexico and sell in the US.
for_you: A weaker peso and rate cuts help the airport stocks (ASR, PAC) more than consumer names. Nothing here is a setup today. Watch only if you want Mexico exposure.

summary: Korea is a memory chip market, and it swings hardest on AI news. After Amazon's cash burn and Intel's weak outlook, the KOSPI fell 3.48% to 5,730.74 on Oct 30, with SK hynix down about 6.4% and Samsung about 3.5% during the session (CNBC). The selloff is about whether AI spenders keep paying, not about memory demand: Samsung and SK hynix both said this week that HBM supply stays tight into 2028 (Reuters). The Bank of Korea held at 3.00% on Oct 22. US investors reach Korea mostly through EWY, the SK hynix ADR (SKHY), Korean bank ADRs and Coupang.
for_you: No chase and no puts on Korea this week. EWY closed at 161.83 on Oct 29, down 2.46%, and SKHY at 162.09 (Massive), before the Oct 30 drop. MU fell 4.98% to 934.27 on Oct 29.

summary: Taiwan's story is the AI chip boom. On Oct 15 TSMC reported Q3 revenue of $46.72 billion, up 41.2%, and guided Q4 to $52.3 to $54.3 billion, saying AI demand is far above supply. But investors now doubt the spenders will keep paying: on Oct 30 the Taiex fell 1,156.50 points, or 2.49%, to 45,211.83, its lowest in over two months, and foreign investors sold a net NT$112.47 billion (Focus Taiwan, Trading Economics). TSMC fell 1.86% to NT$2,370 in Taipei, and its ADR closed at 431.81 on Oct 29, down 1.75% (Focus Taiwan, Massive). The main local risks remain China-Taiwan tension or US chip tariffs; no new tension was found this week.
for_you: No new Taiwan puts or buys while foreigners are selling this hard. TSMC's own guidance has not changed, so this is a price problem, not a business problem, for now.
